title: Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants
summary: Whole-roadmap plan of prismatic cohomology: δ-rings and prisms (PR.0), the relative site and its comparisons (PR.1), derived prismatic cohomology and perfectoidization (PR.2), the Nygaard filtration and Breuil–Kisin twists (PR.3), syntomic complexes and the étale comparison (PR.4), absolute prismatic cohomology and the Cartier–Witt stack (PR.5), q-crystalline cohomology and the AΩ comparison (PR.6), prismatic F-crystals and crystalline lattices (PR.7) and logarithmic prismatic cohomology (PR.8). The two accepted parts (369 nodes) are imported unchanged. This packet adds the seven nodes the upstream order requires: the quasi-coherent complexes on prestacks with flat descent and affine direct image that PR.5 took from LanglandsParameterStacks, the framed q-automorphisms and q-de Rham Koszul complex that PR.6 took from QWittVectors, and two named inputs of PR.7 replacing citations of RefinedTraceMethods and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals, with the re-pointings, dropped stage edges and the PR.8 stage-citation map recorded as restructuring.

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent complexes on a prestack
nodes.statement: Let CRing be the category of commutative rings, and let X be a prestack: a functor from CRing to ∞-groupoids (for the uses here, to groupoids, such as Cart, WCart, WCart^HT, Spf A, BG for an affine group scheme G). Its category of points Pt(X) has objects the pairs (R, η) with η ∈ X(R), equivalently morphisms η : Spec R → X, and morphisms (R, η) → (R′, η′) the ring maps f : R → R′ with an identification X(f)(η) ≃ η′. Let D(R) be the derived ∞-category of R-modules with derived tensor product, and f^* = R′ ⊗^L_R (−) : D(R) → D(R′). The ∞-category of quasi-coherent complexes on X is the limit D(X) := lim_{(R, η) ∈ Pt(X)} D(R), formed in symmetric monoidal ∞-categories. An object F assigns to each point η a complex F_η ∈ D(R) and to each morphism an equivalence R′ ⊗^L_R F_η ≃ F_{η′}, with all higher coherences. Properties: (1) D(Spec R) ≃ D(R), F ↦ F_{id}; for the terminal prestack Spec Z, D(Spec Z) ≃ D(Z). (2) A morphism g : X → Y of prestacks induces a symmetric monoidal, exact, colimit-preserving pullback g^* : D(Y) → D(X), (g^*F)_η = F_{g∘η}, with id^* = id and (h∘g)^* ≃ g^* ∘ h^*. (3) D(X) is stable and admits small colimits, computed pointwise; it is presentable when X is a small colimit of corepresentable prestacks. (4) D sends small colimits of prestacks to limits: D(colim_i X_i) ≃ lim_i D(X_i). (5) A morphism of D(X) is an equivalence if and only if it is one at every point. (6) The unit O_X is (R, η) ↦ R; Perf(X) ⊂ D(X), the full subcategory of F with every F_η perfect, is exactly the subcategory of dualizable objects, and the invertible objects are those with every F_η invertible in D(R).
hypotheses: Rings are ordinary commutative rings; X may take values in large groupoids, so D(X) is a large ∞-category in general (Lurie's convention of not necessarily small spaces).

The limit is a limit of ∞-categories, not of the triangulated homotopy categories: gluing data must include all higher coherences, and the homotopy category of D(X) is not the limit of the homotopy categories of the D(R).

For a functor X defined only on rings in which p is nilpotent (a formal prestack over Spf Z_p, such as WCart), Pt(X) is formed over those rings; this is the same as D of the extension of X by the empty groupoid on the other rings, since the empty prestack has D = 0 (test below).
proofSteps: Construction: apply the straightening of the coCartesian fibration of pairs (R, M ∈ D(R)) over CRing to Pt(X), and take the ∞-category of coCartesian sections; equivalently the right Kan extension of R ↦ D(R) along the Yoneda embedding (Lurie, SAG Definition 6.2.2.1 and Remark 6.2.2.2, with Remark 6.2.2.7 for the pointwise description). The limits of presentable symmetric monoidal ∞-categories used are those of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:presentability/limits-of-presentable-categories.
(1): Pt(Spec R) has the initial object (R, id), so the limit is evaluation there (SAG Remark 6.2.2.5); Spec Z is the terminal prestack because every ring receives a unique map from Z.

(2): precomposition of the limit diagram along Pt(X) → Pt(Y) (SAG Notation 6.2.2.6); (3): every D(R) is stable with colimits and every base change preserves them, so the limit is computed in the subcategory of stable ∞-categories with colimits and colimit-preserving functors (SAG Proposition 6.2.3.4 (1)–(3)).

(4): the right Kan extension of a functor turns colimits of presheaves into limits (SAG Lemma 6.2.1.12 as used in Proposition 6.2.3.1). (5): equivalences in a limit of ∞-categories are detected on the components.

(6): dualizability in a limit of symmetric monoidal ∞-categories along symmetric monoidal functors is detected on the components, and the dualizable objects of D(R) are the perfect complexes (Lurie, HA Proposition 7.2.4.4); invertibility likewise.
acceptance: For X = Spec R the construction returns D(R), and pullback along Spec R′ → Spec R is derived base change.
For X = WCart it returns Bhatt–Lurie's D(WCart) of Definition 3.3.1 verbatim, with O_WCart the unit of Example 3.3.3.

For the classifying stack B(Z/2) over F_2 (the quotient of Spec F_2 by the trivial action of the constant group Z/2), Hom_{D(B(Z/2))}(O, O[1]) ≅ H^1(Z/2, F_2) = F_2, while the pullback to the atlas Spec F_2 kills it.

sources.locator: Definition 6.2.2.1, Remarks 6.2.2.2, 6.2.2.5, 6.2.2.7, Notation 6.2.2.6 (§6.2.2, pp. 490–492 of the February 2018 version)

api.name: QCohPrestack.eval

api.name: QCohPrestack.specEquiv

api.name: QCohPrestack.limitOfColimit

api.name: QCohPrestack.isEquiv_iff_eval
api.statement: A morphism u in D(X) is an equivalence iff eval_η(u) is an equivalence for every point η.

api.name: QCohPrestack.unit_eval
api.statement: (O_X)_η = R for every point η : Spec R → X.

api.name: QCohPrestack.isDualizable_iff_perfect
api.statement: F is dualizable in D(X) iff F_η is perfect for every point; Perf(X) denotes this full subcategory, closed under tensor products and duals.

api.name: QCohPrestack.isInvertible_iff
api.statement: F is invertible in D(X) iff each F_η is invertible in D(R).

api.name: QCohPrestack.homotopyCategory_spec

tests.name: QCohPrestack.empty
tests.statement: For the empty prestack (every X(R) empty) Pt(X) is empty and D(X) is the terminal ∞-category 0; consequently D(WCart) sees no ring in which p is not nilpotent.

tests.name: QCohPrestack.terminal
tests.statement: For the terminal prestack Spec Z, D(Spec Z) ≃ D(Z) and the unit is Z.

tests.name: QCohPrestack.spec_homotopy
tests.statement: For X = Spec R, the homotopy category of D(X) is equivalent to DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R), and Hom(O, O[i]) is R for i = 0 and 0 for i ≠ 0.

tests.name: QCohPrestack.classifying_Z2
tests.statement: For X = B(Z/2) over F_2, Hom_{D(X)}(O, O[1]) = H^1(Z/2, F_2) = F_2 ≠ 0; so D(X) is not D(F_2) of the atlas Spec F_2 → X, and pullback to the atlas is not fully faithful.

tests.name: QCohPrestack.dualizable_spec
tests.statement: In D(Spec Z) the object Z ⊕ Z[3] is dualizable and Q is not (it is not perfect).

nodes.title: Faithfully flat descent for quasi-coherent complexes
nodes.statement: (1) Let R → S be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings, with Čech nerve S^• (S^n = S ⊗_R ⋯ ⊗_R S, n + 1 factors). Base change gives an equivalence of symmetric monoidal ∞-categories D(R) ≃ Tot(D(S^•)) = lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} D(S^n). (2) Consequently, for a morphism of prestacks u : X′ → X that becomes an equivalence after fpqc sheafification (for example X′ → X its fpqc stackification), u^* : D(X) → D(X′) is an equivalence. (3) If X is an fpqc stack and U → X is a morphism of prestacks that is an effective epimorphism of fpqc sheaves (surjective fpqc-locally), with Čech nerve U_• (U_n the (n + 1)-fold fibre power over X), then D(X) ≃ Tot(D(U_•)); the same holds with the Zariski topology in place of the fpqc topology when U → X is a Zariski-local surjection. (4) On the hearts, (1) restricts to faithfully flat descent of modules.
hypotheses: (1): R → S faithfully flat, so every S^n is a discrete ring and every coface map is flat; for non-flat R → S the statement is false (test: Z → F_p).
(3): X is an fpqc (respectively Zariski) stack of ∞-groupoids on commutative rings; the fibre powers U_n need not be affine.
Large prestacks are allowed, as in the construction node.
proofSteps: (1) is the case of discrete rings and flat maps of Lurie's fpqc descent for module ∞-categories (SAG Corollary D.6.3.3); flatness keeps the Čech nerve discrete, so the relative tensor products agree with the ordinary ones.

(2): D sends colimits of prestacks to limits (PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-prestacks (4)); by (1) the functor Spec R ↦ D(R) is an fpqc sheaf of ∞-categories, so D factors through fpqc sheafification (the argument of SAG Proposition 6.2.3.1 and Remark 6.2.3.2).

(3): an effective epimorphism of sheaves is the geometric realization of its Čech nerve, so X ≃ |U_•| after sheafification; apply (2) and the limit property (4) of the construction node. This is the descent step of Bhatt–Lurie Lemma 3.3.10 (Zariski) and of the proof of Proposition 3.3.5 (flat).
(4): truncate to discrete objects and compare with SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/qcoh-fpqc-descent.
acceptance: For X = WCart and the Zariski surjection Spf(A^0) → WCart with fibre powers Spf(A^n), (3) gives Bhatt–Lurie's equivalence D(WCart) ≃ Tot(D̂(A^•)) (Lemma 3.3.10).
For a finite Galois extension of fields K → L with group G, (1) and (3) give D(K) ≃ D(L)^{hG}, the ∞-categorical form of Galois descent.
Non-example: for Z → F_p (not flat), Tot(D(F_p^{⊗•})) is not D(Z); for instance Q is killed by base change.

sources.locator: Corollary D.6.3.3 (Appendix D.6.3, p. 1943 of the February 2018 version)
sources.match: Module ∞-categories satisfy descent for the fpqc topology on E∞-rings; the discrete flat case is statement (1).
The quasi-coherent ∞-category of a functor is unchanged by fpqc sheafification and turns limits of fpqc sheaves into limits.

nodes.title: Direct image along affine morphisms of prestacks, base change and projection formula
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be an affine morphism of prestacks: for every point η : Spec R → X the fibre product Y ×_X Spec R is equivalent to Spec B_η for an R-algebra B_η, compatibly with base change. Then: (a) f^* : D(X) → D(Y) has a right adjoint f_* : D(Y) → D(X), computed pointwise, (f_*G)_η = G restricted to Spec B_η and regarded as an R-complex by restriction of scalars along R → B_η; (b) base change: for every g : X′ → X with pullback f′ : Y′ → X′ and g′ : Y′ → Y, the canonical map g^* f_* → f′_* g′^* is an equivalence; (c) f_* preserves small colimits and satisfies the projection formula F ⊗ f_*G ≃ f_*(f^*F ⊗ G) for F ∈ D(X), G ∈ D(Y); (d) for any prestack X the functor D(Z) → D(X), M ↦ M ⊗ O_X, has a right adjoint RΓ(X, −), and when X ≃ |U_•| with U_n = Spf or Spec of rings as in the descent node, RΓ(X, F) ≃ Tot(RΓ(U_•, F|U_•)).
hypotheses: Affineness is the hypothesis of (a)–(c): for non-affine f the pointwise formula fails and f_* is in general not compatible with base change.

In (d) RΓ exists for every prestack because M ↦ M ⊗ O_X preserves colimits between presentable ∞-categories; presentability of D(X) uses that X is a small colimit of corepresentables, which holds for the stacks used here (they have Čech atlases by affine formal schemes).
proofSteps: (a), (b): for X = Spec R this is restriction of scalars along R → B, right adjoint to base change, and the base change map is the associativity equivalence R′ ⊗^L_R M ≃ (R′ ⊗^L_R B) ⊗^L_B M; in general define f_* pointwise and check, using base change for affine schemes, that the pointwise objects form a compatible family (Lurie, SAG Proposition 6.3.4.1, which treats the more general quasi-compact quasi-separated relative algebraic spaces).
(c): reduce by (b) to X = Spec R, where f_* is restriction of scalars and both claims are elementary (SAG Corollary 6.3.4.3).
(d): adjoint functor theorem for presentable ∞-categories; on a Čech atlas combine the descent node (3) with (a) for the affine maps U_n → X. This is Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 3.3.11 for WCart.
acceptance: For ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart of a bounded prism (affine by PR.5/wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms (2)), ρ_{A*} exists and commutes with base change along any point of WCart.
For X = WCart, RΓ(WCart, F) = Tot(F(A^•)) on the Čech nerve of the universal oriented prism, with values in derived p-complete complexes (Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 3.3.11).
Non-example: for the non-affine projection P^1_Z → Spec Z, the pointwise formula is wrong: H^1 contributions of O(−2) are invisible to restriction of scalars of global sections.

sources.match: Existence of the direct image right adjoint, base change for quasi-compact quasi-separated relative algebraic spaces, colimit preservation and the projection formula.
Global sections on the Cartier–Witt stack as right adjoint, computed as a totalization on the Čech nerve.

nodes.title: Framed algebras and their q-automorphisms
nodes.statement: Let D be a commutative ring with an element q, and let I = (q − 1) or I = (p, q − 1). Let P be a derived I-complete D-algebra and (X_s)_{s ∈ S} elements of P such that the framing □ : D[X_s : s ∈ S]^∧_I → P is I-completely ind-étale (an étale framing; a toric framing has the X_s units and D[X_s^{±1}]^∧_I as source). Assume P is (q − 1)-torsion-free and each X_s is a nonzerodivisor on P (as for the framed q-PD data of PR.6, where P is flat over Z_p[[q − 1]]). Then: (1) there are unique D-algebra automorphisms γ_s (s ∈ S) of P with γ_s(□(X_t)) = q^{δ_{st}} X_t and γ_s ≡ id modulo (q − 1); they commute pairwise, and γ_s(f) − f ∈ (q − 1)X_s P for every f ∈ P; (2) they are functorial for maps of framed algebras (P, S) → (P′, S′) given by a D-algebra map and an injective map S → S′ compatible with the coordinates; (3) if D is a δ-ring with δ(q) = 0, I = (p, q − 1), and D is p-torsion-free, there is a unique δ-D-algebra structure on P with δ(X_s) = 0 (Frobenius φ_□ with φ_□(X_s) = X_s^p), and φ_□ ∘ γ_s = γ_s ∘ φ_□.
hypotheses: Completeness is for the I-adic topology with q − 1 ∈ I: the extension of γ_s uses that γ_s on D[X_s]^∧ is congruent to the identity modulo the topologically nilpotent q − 1; it fails for a framing that is only p-completely étale with I = (p) (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E65 of the accepted part records the same point for BS22 §16).
Nonzerodivisor hypotheses: (q − 1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor on P, so the quotients in the next node are unique.
(3) needs the Frobenius lift of D to fix q up to φ(q) = q^p, which δ(q) = 0 gives.
proofSteps: Polynomial case: on D[X_s]^∧ define γ_s by X_s ↦ qX_s and X_t ↦ X_t; it is congruent to the identity modulo (q − 1) and γ_s(X^m) − X^m = (q^{m_s} − 1)X^m ∈ (q − 1)X_s D[X]^∧.

Extension: γ_s ∘ □ and □ agree modulo (q − 1); since □ is I-completely ind-étale and P is derived (q − 1)-complete (as q − 1 ∈ I), the map γ_s ∘ □ extends uniquely to an endomorphism of P lifting the identity modulo (q − 1) (Bhatt–Scholze Construction 16.19; Scholze, Canonical q-deformations §3, p. 6, for D = Z[[q − 1]] and §4, p. 8, for A_inf with q = [ε]); uniqueness gives γ_s γ_t = γ_t γ_s and invertibility (γ_s^{-1} is the extension of X_s ↦ q^{-1}X_s when q is a unit, which it is in the I-complete ring D).

Divisibility by (q − 1)X_s: the endomorphism f ↦ γ_s(f) − f is a γ_s-twisted derivation; it vanishes on the coordinates X_t (t ≠ s) and sends X_s to (q − 1)X_s, so on D[X]^∧ it takes values in (q − 1)X_s; on P use that γ_s and the identity induce two D[X]^∧-algebra maps P → P/(q − 1)X_sP that agree modulo q − 1, and uniqueness of lifts along the I-completely ind-étale framing (P being derived (q − 1)-complete) makes them equal (Bhatt–Scholze Construction 16.20 uses this divisibility to define the q-derivatives).
(3): extend δ(X_s) = 0 along the I-completely ind-étale framing (Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.18 through PR.0/delta-etale-extension); γ_s is a δ-map on D[X]^∧ since δ(qX_s) = 0, hence on P by uniqueness.
acceptance: For P = D[X]^∧ with one coordinate, γ(X^m) = q^m X^m for m ≥ 0.
Modulo q − 1 every γ_s is the identity, so all structure collapses to the plain framed algebra P/(q − 1).

sources.match: For a framed algebra over a q-PD pair, the automorphisms scaling one coordinate by q extend uniquely along the completely étale framing and commute.
Defines the automorphisms γ_i of the (q−1)-completed polynomial ring scaling T_i by q, lifts them along an étale framing using (q−1)-adic completeness, and does the same over A_inf with q = [ε].

nodes.title: q-derivatives and the framed q-de Rham Koszul complex
nodes.statement: Let E be a commutative ring with an element q, elements X_s (s ∈ S) and pairwise commuting ring automorphisms γ_s with γ_s(X_t) = q^{δ_st}X_t, such that γ_s(f) − f ∈ (q − 1)X_s E for all f and every (q − 1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor (for instance E = P a framed algebra of the previous node, or its q-PD envelope). (1) The q-derivative ∇_{q,s}(f) is the unique element with (q − 1)X_s·∇_{q,s}(f) = γ_s(f) − f. It is additive, kills the elements fixed by γ_s, satisfies the twisted Leibniz rule ∇_{q,s}(fg) = ∇_{q,s}(f)g + γ_s(f)∇_{q,s}(g), ∇_{q,s}(X_s^n) = [n]_q X_s^{n−1} with [n]_q = 1 + q + ⋯ + q^{n−1}, and ∇_{q,s}∇_{q,t} = ∇_{q,t}∇_{q,s}. (2) The framed q-de Rham complex qΩ^{•,□}_E is the Koszul complex of the commuting endomorphisms (∇_{q,s})_{s ∈ S}: qΩ^i = E ⊗ Λ^i(⊕_s Z·dX_s) with differential f·ω ↦ Σ_s ∇_{q,s}(f) dX_s ∧ ω (completed when S is infinite); it is a complex of modules over the γ-invariants of E. (3) Functoriality for ring maps E → E′ commuting with the γ_s and carrying X_s to coordinates of E′ injectively. (4) Reduction: if E = P is a framed algebra over D, the complex modulo q − 1 is the completed de Rham complex Ω^•_{(P/(q−1))/(D/(q−1))}. (5) Toric form: if the X_s are units, qΩ^{•,□} is isomorphic to the Koszul complex of the logarithmic q-derivatives (γ_s − 1)/(q − 1), that is to η_{(q−1)} of the Koszul complex of the γ_s − 1. (6) Frobenius: if E carries an endomorphism φ commuting with the γ_s, with φ(X_s) = X_s^p and φ(q) = q^p, then ∇_{q,s} ∘ φ = [p]_q X_s^{p−1}·φ ∘ ∇_{q,s}.
hypotheses: (q − 1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor on E for every s; without this ∇_{q,s} is not well defined.
(3) requires injectivity on coordinates: identifying two coordinates does not commute with q-derivatives (test below).
(4) uses that P is flat over D and D is (q − 1)-torsion-free, so reduction commutes with the Koszul construction.
proofSteps: (1): uniqueness and existence from the divisibility hypothesis and the nonzerodivisor; the Leibniz rule from γ_s(fg) − fg = (γ_s(f) − f)g + γ_s(f)(γ_s(g) − g); the monomial formula from γ_s(X_s^n) − X_s^n = (q^n − 1)X_s^n; commutation from the symmetric formula (γ_sγ_t − γ_s − γ_t + 1)(f) = (q − 1)^2 X_s X_t ∇_{q,s}∇_{q,t}(f), using that γ_s fixes X_t for t ≠ s (Scholze, Canonical q-deformations §3, p. 6).
(2): the Koszul complex of commuting endomorphisms of a module (AInfCohomology:AI.1/koszul-products-and-cohomology), applied to the ∇_{q,s}.
(3): a map commuting with γ_s and preserving X_s commutes with ∇_{q,s} by uniqueness in (1).

(4): modulo q − 1, γ_s = 1 + (q − 1)X_s∇_{q,s} shows ∇_{q,s} reduces to a derivation with ∇(X_s) = 1, the partial derivative ∂/∂X_s, which on an étale framing is the de Rham differential (Scholze §3: the q-de Rham complex reduces to the de Rham complex).

(5): multiply the s-th operator by the unit X_s, then apply the décalage identity η_f Kos(g_s) ≅ Kos(g_s/f) (AInfCohomology:AI.1/ideal-decalage-complex). (6): apply φ to (q − 1)X_s∇_{q,s}(f) = γ_s(f) − f and cancel the nonzerodivisor (q − 1)X_s using φ((q − 1)X_s) = [p]_q (q − 1) X_s^p.
acceptance: For E = Z[T^{±1}][[q − 1]] with γ(T) = qT: H^0 = Z[[q − 1]] and H^1 is Z[[q − 1]] (the class of T^{-1}dT) plus the (q − 1)-completed sum over n ∈ Z, n ≠ −1, of Z[[q − 1]]/[n + 1]_q (Scholze §3, p. 6).
Reduction modulo q − 1 of qΩ^{•,□}_{Z[[q−1]][X]} is the de Rham complex Z[X] → Z[X]dX.
The Frobenius identity (6) for f = X: ∇(X^p) = [p]_q X^{p−1}.

sources.match: Defines the q-derivative as the finite q-difference quotient (γ_i(f) − f)/(qT_i − T_i), computes it on monomials as the q-integer times the lower power, forms the framed q-de Rham complex, and records that it reduces modulo q − 1 to the de Rham complex.
The q-de Rham complex of a framed q-PD datum as the Koszul complex of the commuting q-derivations.

uses.how: this Koszul complex applied to the q-PD envelope D_{J,q}(P)
the framed q-de Rham complex of a smooth Z_p-algebra
the q-crystalline and A_inf comparisons are computed by this complex, with the Frobenius of (6)

api.name: QFraming.qDeriv
api.statement: The q-derivative ∇_{q,s} : E → E.

api.name: QFraming.qDeriv_spec
api.statement: (q − 1)X_s ∇_{q,s}(f) = γ_s(f) − f, and ∇_{q,s}(f) is the unique element with this property.

api.name: QFraming.qDeriv_mul
api.statement: Twisted Leibniz: ∇_{q,s}(fg) = ∇_{q,s}(f)g + γ_s(f)∇_{q,s}(g).

api.name: QFraming.qDeriv_X_pow
api.statement: ∇_{q,s}(X_s^{n+1}) = [n + 1]_q X_s^n and ∇_{q,s}(X_t) = 0 for t ≠ s.

api.name: QFraming.qDeRhamComplex
api.statement: The Koszul complex of the commuting ∇_{q,s}.

api.name: QFraming.qDeRhamComplex_map
api.statement: Maps commuting with γ and injective on coordinates induce maps of complexes.

api.name: QFraming.qDeRhamComplex_mod
api.statement: Modulo q − 1 the complex is the completed de Rham complex of P/(q − 1) over D/(q − 1).

api.name: QFraming.qDeRhamComplex_toric
api.statement: For unit coordinates, the complex is η_{(q−1)} of the Koszul complex of the γ_s − 1.

tests.name: QFraming.qDeRham_empty
tests.statement: For S empty there are no q-derivatives and the complex is E in degree 0; for one coordinate it has length one, E → E·dX.

tests.name: QFraming.qDeriv_leibniz_check
tests.statement: ∇_q(X·X) = ∇_q(X)X + γ(X)∇_q(X) = X + qX = (1 + q)X, which is ∇_q(X^2).

tests.name: QFraming.qDeriv_not_untwisted
tests.statement: The untwisted Leibniz rule fails: ∇_q(X)X + X∇_q(X) = 2X ≠ (1 + q)X = ∇_q(X^2) in Z[q][X].

tests.name: QFraming.qDeRham_not_functorial_diagonal
tests.statement: The map D[X_0, X_1] → D[X] sending both coordinates to X (not injective on coordinates) does not commute with q-derivatives: ∇_{q,0}(X_0X_1) = X_1 and ∇_{q,1}(X_0X_1) = X_0, so the image of ∇_q(X_0X_1) is 2X dX, while ∇_q(X^2) = (1 + q)X dX.

nodes.title: The Beilinson fibre square on syntomic complexes (named input)
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R write Q_p(n)(R) = Z_p(n)(R)[1/p] for the syntomic complex of PR.4/syntomic-complex, LΩ_R for the p-completed derived de Rham cohomology of R over Z_p with its Hodge filtration LΩ_R^{≥n} (not Hodge-completed), and (−)_{Q_p} for p-completion followed by inverting p. (i) For every p-torsion-free quasisyntomic ring R and n ≥ 0 there are a natural map χ_n : Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p} and a functorial pullback square in D(Q_p) with top row Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p), left column Q_p(n)(R) → (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p}, right column χ_n and bottom row (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p} → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}; equivalently a fibre sequence Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R/LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p}. (ii) For R quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free and n > 0, χ_n is injective with image the φ = p^n eigenspace of A_crys(R/p)[1/p] = (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}; up to a nonzero scalar depending only on n it is the forgetful map Q_p(n)(R/p) → Δ_{R/p}[1/p] composed with Δ_{R/p} ≅ A_crys(R/p) ≅ LΩ_R. (iii) Check: for R = O_C the sequence on H^0 is 0 → Q_p(n) → (B_crys^+)^{φ = p^n} → B_dR^+/Fil^n → 0 for n ≥ 1. Within this roadmap the statement is a named input: its only consumer, PR.7/tate-twist-analytic-continuation, is proved from it, and its proof (through topological cyclic homology) lies outside the roadmaps this roadmap builds on.
hypotheses: R p-torsion-free and quasisyntomic in (i); quasiregular semiperfectoid in (ii); n ≥ 0 in (i), n > 0 in (ii).
The order of operations in (−)_{Q_p} matters: complete first, then invert p.

This roadmap does not prove the statement: the proof constructs the square from the pullback square TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p) over HC^-(R; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p) and the motivic filtrations of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, which no roadmap below this one in the upstream order provides; the gap 'Trace-theoretic proof of the Beilinson fibre square' records it.
proofSteps: Outline of the source proof, for the record of the named input: for R quasiregular semiperfectoid the bottom row of the TC/HC^-/HP square is even, so τ_{[2n−1, 2n]} of the square is again a pullback; by the definition of Z_p(n) through the motivic filtration and the description of π_{2n}HC^- and π_{2n}HP by Hodge-completed derived de Rham cohomology this gives a Hodge-completed version of the square; Hodge completion is removed by left Kan extension from polynomial algebras; general quasisyntomic R follows by unfolding (Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, Theorem 6.17 with proof).

(ii): Proposition 6.18 of the same paper, using Corollary 6.20 and the Frobenius action of Lemma 6.19; the identification of their Z_p(n) (defined with topological cyclic homology) with the prismatic syntomic complex is Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 14.1 with Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Theorem 1.12.

(iii): for R = O_C, Q_p(n)(O_C) = Q_p(n)[0] by the étale comparison PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison, Q_p(n)(O_C/p) has H^0 = (A_crys(O_C/p)[1/p])^{φ = p^n} = (B_crys^+)^{φ = p^n} and LΩ_{O_C}/Fil^n ⊗ Q = B_dR^+/Fil^n (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4/rational-hodge-period-comparison).
acceptance: For R = O_C and n = 1: 0 → Q_p(1) → (B_crys^+)^{φ = p} → C → 0, the fundamental exact sequence.
For n = 0 the third term vanishes and the square says Q_p(0)(R) ≃ Q_p(0)(R/p).
Consumed exactly once: PR.7/tate-twist-analytic-continuation, steps 2–3.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.17 with proof, Proposition 6.18, Lemma 6.19, Corollary 6.20 (§6, pp. 44–46 of the arXiv version)
sources.match: Constructs the natural map from the rationalized weight-n syntomic complex of R/p to rationalized derived de Rham cohomology and the pullback square on graded pieces, for p-torsion-free quasisyntomic R; identifies the image of that map for quasiregular semiperfectoid R as the Frobenius eigenspace of slope n.
Uses the fibre square of graded pieces and the description of the map as the input of the analytic continuation of Tate twists.

nodes.title: Triviality of the slope-zero bundle of a weakly admissible module (named input)
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, A_inf = W(O_C^♭), X_FF the Fargues–Fontaine curve of C^♭ (the adic curve of Tau Ceti's AdicSpaces roadmap, Layer 6) and ℛ the Robba ring of A_inf (the extended Robba ring of the Berkeley lectures). (i) The category of φ-modules over ℛ is equivalent to the category of vector bundles on X_FF, compatibly with tensor products and duals. (ii) For a weakly admissible filtered φ-module (D, φ_D, Fil^•) over a complete discretely valued K ⊂ C with perfect residue field, the bundle E(D, φ_D, Fil^•) obtained from E(D, φ_D) by modification at ∞ along the B_dR^+-lattice Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR) is semistable of slope 0. (iii) A semistable vector bundle of slope 0 on X_FF is trivial, i.e. isomorphic to O_X^r. Consequently the φ-module over ℛ attached to a weakly admissible (D, φ_D, Fil^•) is trivial: it has a φ-fixed basis. Within this roadmap the statement is a named input of PR.7/weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf; its proof (the classification of vector bundles on X_FF) lies outside the roadmaps this roadmap builds on.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed: (iii) fails over a non-algebraically-closed perfectoid field without Galois descent.
Weak admissibility in the sense of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility, with the filtration on D ⊗_{W(k), φ} K as in the consumer.
This roadmap does not prove the statement; the gap 'Classification of vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve' records it.
proofSteps: Outline of the source proofs, for the record of the named input: (i) by Fargues–Fontaine Corollary 11.2.22, gluing φ-modules over the Robba ring along the Frobenius quotient of the punctured open disc; (ii) by Proposition 10.5.6, computing degrees of sub-bundles through the Hodge and Newton polygons; (iii) by Theorem 8.2.10 (1), the slope-zero case of the classification of vector bundles by slopes.
Consequence: combine (i)–(iii); the φ-fixed basis of the trivial bundle is a φ-fixed basis of the φ-module.
acceptance: For D = K_0 with φ_D = σ and the trivial filtration, the bundle is O_X and the φ-module is ℛ with its Frobenius: trivially trivial.

For D = D_cris(V) of a crystalline representation V (for instance V = Q_p(1), D = K_0 e with φ(e) = p^{-1}e and Fil^{-1} = D_K, Fil^0 = 0), the modified bundle is V ⊗_{Q_p} O_X, trivial of slope 0, as (ii)–(iii) predict.
Consumed exactly once: PR.7/weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf, steps 1–2.

sources.locator: Corollary 11.2.22, Proposition 10.5.6, Theorem 8.2.10 (1), as cited in Bhatt–Scholze, Prismatic F-crystals, §6.4
sources.match: The φ-module/vector bundle dictionary over the Robba ring, the slope-zero semistability of the bundle of a weakly admissible filtered φ-module, and the triviality of semistable slope-zero bundles; the locators are those the F-crystals paper prints.

sources.locator: Section 6.4, proof of essential surjectivity, second paragraph
sources.match: Applies the three results to show that the φ-module over the Robba ring attached to a weakly admissible module is trivial.
